translations.literal: He was also demoted for failure to detect heterodox sects while serving as surveillance commissioner, and was reassigned to the Tianjin Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was further demoted for failing to detect heterodox sects during his tenure as surveillance commissioner and was reassigned to the Tianjin Circuit.

sentences.zh: 再授浙江布政使。

translations.literal: He was once more appointed Financial Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Financial Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢江蘇巡撫，免沛縣昭陽湖淹地老荒麻地徵課。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Governor of Jiangsu and exempted old wasteland hemp fields inundated by Zhaoyang Lake in Pei County from taxation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Governor of Jiangsu and exempted long-abandoned hemp fields flooded by Zhaoyang Lake in Pei County from taxation.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died shortly thereafter.

sentences.zh: 子亶望，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Danwang has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Danwang has his own biography.

sentences.zh: =尹會一=尹會一，字元孚，直隸博野人。

translations.literal: Yin Huiyi, style Yuanfu, a native of Boye in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Huiyi, courtesy name Yuanfu, was a native of Boye in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年進士，分工部學習，授主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Yongzheng, he was assigned to study in the Ministry of Works, appointed secretary, and promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Yongzheng reign, was assigned to train in the Ministry of Works, appointed secretary, and then promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為襄陽知府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he went out and became Prefect of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Prefect of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 漢水暴漲，壞護城石堤。

translations.literal: The Han River rose violently and destroyed the stone embankment protecting the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Han River rose in flood and destroyed the stone embankment protecting the city walls.

sentences.zh: 會一督修建，分植巡功，民忘其勞。

translations.literal: Huiyi personally supervised the rebuilding, divided the work and inspected progress, and the people forgot their toil.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Huiyi personally supervised the repairs, dividing the labor and inspecting progress, so that the people scarcely felt the burden.

sentences.zh: 創八蜡廟，表諸葛亮所居山，復為茅廬其上。

translations.literal: He founded a temple to the Eight Agricultural Deities, marked the mountain where Zhuge Liang had lived, and restored a thatched hut upon it.
translations.idiomatic: He built a temple to the Eight Agricultural Deities, marked the mountain where Zhuge Liang had lived, and restored a thatched hut on the summit.

sentences.zh: 署荊州，石首饑民聚眾，揚言將劫倉穀。

translations.literal: While acting as prefect of Jingzhou, hungry people in Shishou gathered in a crowd and declared they would plunder the granary.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as acting Prefect of Jingzhou, hungry people in Shishou gathered in a mob and threatened to loot the public granary.

sentences.zh: 會一單騎往諭，係其強悍者，發倉穀次第散予之，眾悅服。

translations.literal: Huiyi went alone on horseback to instruct them, detained the ringleaders, opened the granary and distributed grain to them in turn, and the crowd submitted in satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Huiyi rode out alone to reason with them, detained the ringleaders, opened the granary, and distributed grain in orderly fashion; the crowd submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 九年，調江南揚州知府，濬新舊城巿河通舟楫，濬城西蜀岡下河灌田疇。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Prefect of Yangzhou in Jiangnan, dredged the market canals of the old and new cities to open them to boats, and dredged the river below Shugang west of the city to irrigate the fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Prefect of Yangzhou in Jiangnan, dredged the market canals of the old and new cities to allow passage by boat, and cleared the river below Shugang west of the city to irrigate the farmland.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷兩淮鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Salt Transport Commissioner of the Two Huai Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Salt Transport Commissioner of the Two Huai Circuits.

sentences.zh: 新安定書院，士興於學。

translations.literal: He newly established and stabilized the academy, and scholars flourished in learning.
translations.idiomatic: He restored and strengthened the local academy, and scholarly activity flourished.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，就加僉都御史銜，擢兩淮鹽政。

translations.literal: When Gaozong acceded to the throne, he was at once given the nominal rank of Vice Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Salt Controller of the Two Huai Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor acceded to the throne, Yin Huiyi was immediately granted the nominal rank of Vice Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Salt Controller of the Two Huai Circuits.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，入覲，命署廣東​​巡撫，以母老辭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong he came to audience, was ordered to serve as acting Governor of Guangdong, and declined on account of his aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Qianlong reign he came to court, was ordered to serve as acting Governor of Guangdong, but declined because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 調署河南巡撫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as acting Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to serve as acting Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 河南方閔雨，疏請緩徵，並發倉平糶，不拘存七糶三舊例，視緩急為多寡，上從之。

translations.literal: Henan was then praying for rain; he memorialized requesting deferred tax collection and the opening of granaries for fair-price sale, not bound by the old rule of retaining seventy percent and selling thirty percent, but adjusting the amount according to urgency, and the Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Henan was then suffering drought; he memorialized requesting deferred tax collection and the release of grain from public granaries at fair prices, not bound by the old rule of keeping seventy percent in store and selling only thirty percent, but adjusting quantities according to need; the Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋疏言：「力田貴乘天時。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized, saying: "In diligent farming, what matters is seizing the season.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted another memorial stating: "Successful farming depends on keeping pace with the seasons.

sentences.zh: 河南民時宜播種，尚未舉耜；

translations.literal: The people of Henan, when it was time to sow, had not yet taken up the plow;
translations.idiomatic: When the season for sowing arrived in Henan, the farmers had not yet begun plowing;

sentences.zh: 時宜耘耔，始行播種。

translations.literal: when it was time to weed and harrow, they were only then sowing.
translations.idiomatic: when the season for weeding and harrowing came, they were only then sowing their seed.

sentences.zh: 臣擬分析種植先後，刊諭老農，督率勸勉。

translations.literal: Your servant proposes to analyze the sequence of planting, publish instructions for elderly farmers, and supervise and encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: I propose to set out the proper sequence of planting, publish guidance for experienced farmers, and supervise and encourage compliance.

sentences.zh: 如工本不敷，許借倉穀，秋後補還。

translations.literal: If labor costs are insufficient, permit borrowing grain from the granary to be repaid after the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: If farmers lack sufficient capital for labor, allow them to borrow grain from the public stores and repay it after the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 北方地闊，一夫所耕，自七八十畝至百餘畝，力散工薄。

translations.literal: In the north the land is broad; one man may cultivate from seventy or eighty mu up to more than a hundred mu, so labor is scattered and work is thin.
translations.idiomatic: In the north the land is vast; a single farmer may work anywhere from seventy or eighty mu to more than a hundred, spreading his labor too thin.

sentences.zh: 臣勸諭田主，授田以三十畝為率。

translations.literal: Your servant urges and instructs landowners to allot fields at the rate of thirty mu.
translations.idiomatic: I urge landowners to allot fields at a standard of thirty mu per tenant.

sentences.zh: 分多種之田給無田之人，則遊民亦少。

translations.literal: If excess land is divided and given to those without land, then vagrants will also be fewer.
translations.idiomatic: If excess holdings are divided among the landless, the number of vagrants will also decline.

sentences.zh: 河南多咸鹼沙地，犁去三尺，則咸少而潤澤。

translations.literal: Henan has much saline and alkaline sandy land; if three feet are plowed away, the saltiness diminishes and the soil becomes moist and fertile.
translations.idiomatic: Henan has much saline, alkaline, sandy soil; plowing away the top three feet reduces the salt content and restores fertility.

sentences.zh: 臣責成鄉保就隙地植所宜木，則地無曠土。

translations.literal: Your servant holds village elders and tithing officers responsible for planting suitable trees on vacant land, so that no soil lies idle.
translations.idiomatic: I would hold village elders and tithing officers responsible for planting suitable trees on unused land, so that no ground goes to waste.

sentences.zh: 河南產木棉，而商賈販於江南，民家有機杼者百不得一。

translations.literal: Henan produces cotton, yet merchants sell it in Jiangnan; among households, not one in a hundred has a loom.
translations.idiomatic: Henan produces cotton, yet merchants carry it off to Jiangnan for sale; fewer than one household in a hundred owns a loom.

sentences.zh: 擬動公項製造給領。

translations.literal: He proposed to use public funds to manufacture them and distribute them for use.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed using public funds to manufacture looms and distribute them to households.

sentences.zh: 廣勸婦女，互相仿效。

translations.literal: He broadly encouraged women to imitate one another.
translations.idiomatic: He urged women throughout the province to take up weaving and learn from one another.

sentences.zh: 」上諭之曰：「酌量而行，不可欲速，不可終怠。

translations.literal: " The Emperor instructed him, saying: "Act with measured judgment; do not seek haste, and do not end in slackness.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor replied: "Proceed with discretion. Do not rush, but do not grow slack in the end either.

sentences.zh: 若民不樂從，尤不可繩以法也。

translations.literal: If the people are unwilling to follow, all the more must one not bind them with the law.
translations.idiomatic: If the people are unwilling to comply, you must above all avoid coercing them by law.

sentences.zh: 」旋命實授。

translations.literal: " He was soon ordered formally appointed.
translations.idiomatic: " Shortly afterward he was formally appointed to the post.

sentences.zh: 三年，上以河南歲稔，敕籌備倉穀。

translations.literal: In the third year, because Henan had a good harvest, the Emperor ordered preparations of granary grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, noting Henan's good harvest, the Emperor ordered preparations to fill the public granaries.

sentences.zh: 會一疏言：「河南歲豐，直隸、江南歲歉，商販紛集，米價日昂。

translations.literal: Huiyi memorialized, saying: "Henan has a bountiful year while Zhili and Jiangnan have lean years; merchants gather in crowds and the price of rice rises daily.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Huiyi memorialized: "Henan has had a bumper harvest while Zhili and Jiangnan have suffered poor harvests; merchants have flocked in and grain prices rise daily.

sentences.zh: 臣飭有司，本地價高，於鄰縣買補；

translations.literal: Your servant has ordered local officials that where local prices are high, grain be purchased in neighboring counties to make up the shortfall;
translations.idiomatic: I have instructed local officials that where prices are high in one district, grain should be purchased in neighboring counties to make up the deficit;

sentences.zh: 鄰縣價高，報明不敷銀，在各屬盈餘款內均撥。

translations.literal: where neighboring counties also have high prices, report that funds are insufficient and allocate evenly from surplus funds within the subordinate districts.
translations.idiomatic: where neighboring counties also have high prices, report the shortfall in funds and allocate the difference evenly from surplus revenues within the province.

sentences.zh: 河南民食麥為上，高粱、蕎麥、豆次之。

translations.literal: The people of Henan take wheat as primary food, with sorghum, buckwheat, and beans next.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Henan rely chiefly on wheat, with sorghum, buckwheat, and beans as secondary staples.

sentences.zh: 臣並令參酌糴貯，來春先侭糶借。

translations.literal: Your servant also ordered officials to weigh purchase and storage, and in the coming spring first to sell and lend as needed.
translations.idiomatic: I have also ordered officials to purchase and store grain as appropriate, so that in the coming spring it may first be sold or lent out as needed.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor commended this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor praised the proposal.

sentences.zh: 四年，黃河、沁水共漲，瀕河四十七州縣成災。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Yellow River and the Qin River rose together, and forty-seven prefectures and counties along the rivers suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Yellow River and the Qin River flooded together, bringing disaster to forty-seven prefectures and counties along their banks.

sentences.zh: 會一定賑恤規條十六，無食者予一月之糧，無居者予葺屋之資，緩徵減糶​​，留漕運貸倉米，米不足，移他郡之粟助之，富民周濟；

translations.literal: Huiyi fixed sixteen rules for relief and succor: those without food were given one month's grain; those without shelter were given funds to repair houses; tax collection was deferred and grain prices reduced; grain transport was retained and granary rice lent out; where rice was insufficient, grain from other prefectures was moved to assist; the wealthy were urged to give relief;
translations.idiomatic: Yin Huiyi established sixteen rules for relief: the hungry received a month's rations; the homeless received funds to repair their dwellings; tax collection was deferred and grain prices reduced; transport grain was retained and public rice lent out; where supplies ran short, grain was brought in from other prefectures; and the wealthy were urged to contribute;

sentences.zh: 並假餘屋以棲貧窶，建棚舍，安流亡，免米稅，興工代賑，種蔓菁助民食，助耔種，施藥餌，延諸生稽察；

translations.literal: he also borrowed spare houses to shelter the destitute, built sheds, settled refugees, exempted rice from tax, launched public works in place of relief, planted turnips to supplement the people's food, assisted with seed for late planting, dispensed medicine, and employed scholars to inspect and supervise;
translations.idiomatic: spare buildings were lent to shelter the destitute, sheds were erected for refugees, rice taxes were waived, public works were launched as relief, turnips were planted to supplement food supplies, seed was provided for late planting, medicine was distributed, and scholars were enlisted to supervise relief efforts;

sentences.zh: 又令離鄉求食者，有司隨在廩給，開以作業，俟改歲東作資送還鄉。

translations.literal: he further ordered that for those who left their villages seeking food, local officials wherever they were should provide rations, open opportunities for work, and when the year changed and spring plowing came, supply funds to send them home.
translations.idiomatic: he also ordered that refugees seeking food away from home be given rations wherever they were found, offered work, and when the new year came and spring planting began, provided with funds to return home.

sentences.zh: 御史宮煥文劾會一本年報盜百六十餘案，秋審招冊駁改至三十餘案，疲玩貽誤，上以會一忠厚謹慎，非有心誤公，召授左副都御史。

translations.literal: Censor Gong Huanwen impeached Huiyi for reporting more than one hundred and sixty robbery cases in the year while the autumn review registers were rejected and revised down to more than thirty cases, showing negligence and delay; the Emperor, considering Huiyi honest, sincere, and careful, and not deliberately failing in public duty, summoned and appointed him Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Gong Huanwen impeached Yin Huiyi for reporting more than one hundred and sixty robbery cases in a single year while the autumn review registers were cut back to little more than thirty, accusing him of negligence and delay; the Emperor, believing Yin Huiyi to be honest and conscientious rather than deliberately remiss, summoned him and appointed him Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「人主一言，天下屬耳目。

translations.literal: He memorialized, stating: "One word from the sovereign, and the whole realm turns its eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial stating: "A single word from the sovereign is watched and heard throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 今方甄別年老不勝任之員，而饒州知府張鍾以年老改部屬，旬日間前後頓殊，群下無所法守。

translations.literal: Now officials aged and unfit for office are being screened out, yet Prefect Zhang Zhong of Raozhou was transferred to a ministry post on account of age; within ten days the treatment before and after was suddenly different, and subordinates have no standard to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The court is now screening out officials who are too old to serve effectively, yet Prefect Zhang Zhong of Raozhou was transferred to a ministry post on grounds of age; within ten days the policy reversed itself, leaving officials with no consistent standard to follow.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉納之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor commended the memorial and accepted its advice.

sentences.zh: 會一母年七十餘，疏請終養。

translations.literal: Huiyi's mother was more than seventy years old; he memorialized requesting leave to care for her until her death.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Huiyi's mother was over seventy; he memorialized requesting leave to care for her until her death.

sentences.zh: 上知會一孝母，母李先以節孝旌，有賢名，賜詩褒之。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew Huiyi was filial toward his mother; his mother Li had earlier been honored for chastity and filial piety and had a reputation for virtue; he bestowed a poem in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yin Huiyi to be devoted to his mother—whose surname was Li and who had already been honored for chastity and filial devotion and enjoyed a reputation for virtue—the Emperor bestowed a poem in praise.

sentences.zh: 會一在官有善政，必歸美於母。

translations.literal: Whenever Huiyi had good policies in office, he always attributed the credit to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yin Huiyi achieved good results in office, he always credited his mother.

sentences.zh: 家居設義倉，置義田，興義學，謂皆出母意。

translations.literal: At home he established a charity granary, set up charity fields, and founded a charity school, saying all sprang from his mother's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: At home he established a charity granary, endowed charity fields, and founded a charity school, saying that all of this reflected his mother's wishes.

sentences.zh: 母卒，會一年已逾五十，居喪一遵古禮。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Huiyi was already past fifty; in mourning he wholly followed the ancient rites.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death, though Yin Huiyi was already over fifty, he observed mourning in strict accordance with ancient rites.

sentences.zh: 十一年，服闋，召授工部侍郎，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when mourning ended, he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Works and Educational Commissioner of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when his mourning period ended, he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Works and Educational Commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 十二年，上敕各省學政按試時，以御纂四經取與舊說別異處發問，答不失指者，童入學，生補廩。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Emperor ordered that when provincial educational commissioners conducted examinations, they question candidates on points where the imperially compiled Four Classics differ from old interpretations; those whose answers do not miss the point may enter school as licentiates or receive stipends as sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Emperor ordered that when provincial educational commissioners held examinations, they question candidates on points where the imperially compiled Four Classics differ from earlier interpretations; those who answer correctly may be enrolled as licentiates or granted stipends as sheng.

sentences.zh: 會一請令生童冊報考試經解，別期發問，不在冊報者，不概補經解。

translations.literal: Huiyi requested that licentiates and candidates register in lists for examination on classical commentary, with questioning on a separate date; those not on the register should not all be granted classical commentary stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Huiyi proposed that licentiates and candidates register for examination on classical commentary, with questioning held on a separate occasion; those not on the register should not automatically receive stipends for classical commentary.

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the ministry for deliberation and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the ministry for review and approved.

sentences.zh: 會一以江南文勝，風以質行。

translations.literal: Huiyi, taking Jiangnan's literary excellence, used plain conduct to transform custom.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Huiyi emphasized Jiangnan's strength in letters and set an example of unadorned conduct to reform local mores.

sentences.zh: 嘗謁東林道南祠，刻小學頒示士子。

translations.literal: He once visited the Donglin Dao Nan shrine, carved the Elementary Learning, and issued it to scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He once paid respects at the Donglin shrine to Dao Nan, had the Elementary Learning printed, and distributed it among the literati.

sentences.zh: 處士是鏡廬墓隱舜山，親訪之，薦於朝。

translations.literal: The recluse Shi Jing, dwelling in mourning by the tomb in seclusion at Shun Mountain, he personally visited him and recommended him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Shi Jing was living in mourning by his father's tomb in seclusion on Shun Mountain; Yin Huiyi visited him in person and recommended him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 侍郎方苞屏居清涼山，徒步造訪，執弟子禮。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Fang Bao was living in retirement on Qingliang Mountain; he went on foot to visit him and performed the rites of a disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Fang Bao was living in seclusion on Qingliang Mountain; Yin Huiyi walked there to visit him and treated him with the deference due a teacher.

sentences.zh: 校文詳慎，士林悅服。

translations.literal: In grading examination papers he was thorough and careful, and the scholarly community was pleased and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: He examined papers with painstaking care, and men of letters were won over.

sentences.zh: 十三年，轉吏部，仍留學政任。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was transferred to the Board of Personnel but retained his post as educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to the Board of Personnel while remaining educational commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 力疾按試，至松江，卒。

translations.literal: He forced himself to continue conducting examinations despite illness; upon reaching Songjiang, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on with the tour of examination despite illness, he died upon reaching Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 遺疏請任賢納諫。

translations.literal: In his final memorial he requested that worthy men be employed and remonstrance accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In a deathbed memorial he urged the appointment of worthy men and the acceptance of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 巡撫雅爾哈善奏准入名宦祠。

translations.literal: Governor Yarhašan memorialized requesting his admission to the shrine of notable officials.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yarhašan memorialized that he be admitted to the local shrine of eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 子嘉銓，自舉人授刑部主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: His son Jia Quan, from juren was appointed a secretary in the Board of Punishments and was twice promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jia Quan entered service as a secretary in the Board of Punishments after receiving his juren degree and was twice promoted to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 授山東濟東道，再仙甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: He was appointed intendant of Jidong in Shandong, then transferred to Gansu as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed intendant of Jidong in Shandong and later transferred to serve as provincial treasurer of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 改大理寺卿，休致。

translations.literal: Transferred to chief judge of the Court of Revision, then retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief judge of the Court of Revision and then retired.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十六年，上巡幸保定，嘉銓遣其子齎奏，為會一乞諡；

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year of Qianlong, when the Emperor was on tour to Baoding, Jia Quan sent his son to present a memorial requesting a posthumous title for Huiyi;
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year of Qianlong, while the Emperor was touring Baoding, Jia Quan sent his son to submit a memorial asking a posthumous title for Yin Huiyi;

sentences.zh: 又請以湯斌、範文程、李光地、顧八代、張伯行及會一從祀孔子廟。

translations.literal: He also requested that Tang Bin, Fan Wencheng, Li Guangdi, Gu Baidai, Zhang Boxing, and Huiyi be enshrined in the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Tang Bin, Fan Wencheng, Li Guangdi, Gu Baidai, Zhang Boxing, and Yin Huiyi be granted posthumous worship in the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 上責其謬妄，逮至京師親鞫之，坐極刑，改絞死。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked him for his presumptuous error, had him brought to the capital for personal interrogation, sentenced him to the extreme penalty, which was commuted to death by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor denounced his presumption, had him brought to the capital for trial in person, sentenced him to death, and then commuted the sentence to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 上以嘉銓自著年譜，載與刑部簽商緩決，並稱大學士為「相國」，又編本朝名臣言行錄，屢降旨深斥之。

translations.literal: Because Jia Quan had compiled his own chronological biography recording how he consulted with the Board of Punishments on delayed execution, also referred to grand secretaries as "prime minister," and compiled Records of the Words and Deeds of Famous Ministers of Our Dynasty, the Emperor repeatedly issued edicts sharply condemning him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor further condemned Jia Quan for having written his own chronological biography, in which he recorded bargaining with the Board of Punishments over a delayed execution, addressed grand secretaries as "prime minister," and compiled a record of famous ministers' words and deeds—issuing repeated edicts to rebuke him sharply.

sentences.zh: =王恕=王恕，字中安，四川銅梁人。

translations.literal: Wang Shu, courtesy name Zhong'an, a native of Tongliang in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu, courtesy name Zhong'an, was a native of Tongliang in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 康熙六十年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixtieth year of Kangxi, he became a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixtieth year of Kangxi and entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，吏部以員外郎缺員，請以庶吉士揀補，恕與焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, the Board of Personnel, finding a vacancy for bureau vice director, requested that bachelor members of the Hanlin be selected to fill it; Shu was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng, when the Board of Personnel reported a vacancy for bureau vice director and asked that Hanlin bachelors be selected to fill it, Wang Shu was chosen.

sentences.zh: 旋自員外郎遷郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted from bureau vice director to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted from bureau vice director to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 考選廣西道御史。

translations.literal: Selected through examination as censor of the Guangxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected by examination and appointed censor of the Guangxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 轉兵科給事中。

translations.literal: Transferred to supervising secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervising secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 出為江南江安糧道，再遷廣東布政使。

translations.literal: He went out as grain intendant of Jiang'an in Jiangnan, then was again promoted to provincial treasurer of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grain intendant of Jiang'an in Jiangnan and later promoted to provincial treasurer of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五年，署福建巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianlong, he served as acting governor of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qianlong he served as acting governor of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 上諭之曰：「勉力務實，勿粉飾外觀。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed him: "Strive earnestly for practical results; do not embellish outward appearance.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor instructed him: "Work hard at practical results and do not dress up appearances.

sentences.zh: 封疆大吏不可徒自立無過之地，遂謂可保祿全身也。

translations.literal: A territorial high official cannot simply establish for himself a position of being without fault and then suppose he can preserve his salary and keep his person safe."
translations.idiomatic: A frontier governor cannot simply carve out a blameless position for himself and then imagine that he can keep his salary and save his skin."

sentences.zh: 」旋奏：「臣到任數月，官方民俗，積儲兵防，已得其大略。

translations.literal: " Soon he memorialized: "Your servant has been in office several months and has obtained a general grasp of official practice, local custom, stored reserves, and military defense.
translations.idiomatic: " He soon memorialized: "In the few months since I took office I have gained a general understanding of official practice, local custom, stored reserves, and military defense.

sentences.zh: 漳、泉素刁悍，已嚴諭有司勤為聽斷，力行整刷。

translations.literal: Zhangzhou and Quanzhou have always been sharp and fierce; I have already sternly instructed the local officials to hear cases diligently and vigorously rectify abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzhou and Quanzhou have long been unruly; I have already sternly ordered local officials to hear cases diligently and push hard for reform.

sentences.zh: 民俗尚華靡，督臣德沛以儉樸化民，臣更當倡導為助。

translations.literal: Local custom still favors extravagant display; Governor De Pei is transforming the people through frugality and plainness, and your servant should all the more promote and assist this.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom still favors extravagance; Governor-General De Pei is reforming the people through frugality, and I should do all I can to support him.

sentences.zh: 合省常平倉穀，至四年歲終，共存一百三十四萬，又收捐監穀十五萬，委道府切實察覈。

translations.literal: The ever-normal granary grain throughout the province, by the end of the fourth year, totaled 1.34 million [shi] in storage; an additional 150,000 [shi] were collected from purchase-for-student-status donations; these were entrusted to the intendants and prefects for rigorous inspection and verification.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the fourth year the province's ever-normal granaries held 1.34 million shi in all, with another 150,000 shi collected through purchase-for-supervisor donations; I have entrusted the intendants and prefects to inspect these accounts rigorously.

sentences.zh: 」報聞。

translations.literal: " The report was noted.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was noted.

sentences.zh: 六年，奏言：「台灣各縣最稱難治。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he memorialized: "The counties of Taiwan are the most difficult to govern.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he memorialized: "Taiwan's counties are the hardest to govern.

sentences.zh: 於繁缺知縣內揀選調補，多以處分被駁。

translations.literal: When selecting replacements from among magistrates of difficult posts, many are rejected because of pending disciplinary cases.
translations.idiomatic: When replacements are chosen from magistrates holding difficult posts, many candidates are rejected because of pending disciplinary cases.

sentences.zh: 請嗣後調台官員，雖有經徵承追各案，准予題調。

translations.literal: I request that hereafter, when transferring officials to Taiwan, even if they have cases of tax collection arrears or pursuit of unpaid levies, they may be proposed for transfer.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter officials transferred to Taiwan may be proposed for appointment even when they have outstanding cases of tax collection or pursuit of arrears.

sentences.zh: 」上諭曰：「用此定例則不可，隨本奏請則可。

translations.literal: " The Emperor instructed: "To use this as a fixed rule would not do; to request it case by case in each memorial would be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor replied: "This cannot be made a standing rule, but it may be requested case by case in each memorial.

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「各鄉社穀向俱借存寺廟，請於四鄉村鎮適中處分建倉房，工費即以社穀撥充，俟將來續收補項。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Community grain from each township and society has always been stored on loan in temples; I request that at suitable central points in the four township villages and market towns, granary buildings be built separately, the construction costs to be covered from the community grain, to be replenished from future continued collections.
translations.idiomatic: " He also memorialized: "Grain from local community societies has always been stored on loan in temples. I ask that granaries be built at suitable central points in townships and market towns, the construction costs to be paid from the society grain and made up from future collections.

sentences.zh: 」又奏免崇安無田浮賦一千二百五十一頃，及閩縣加徵無著學租。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized to exempt 1,251 qing of floating tax assessment on landless fields in Chong'an, and the additional levy on unassigned school rent in Min County.
translations.idiomatic: " He also memorialized for exemption of 1,251 qing of tax assessed on nonexistent land in Chong'an and of the additional levy on unassigned school rent in Min County.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「福建多山田，零星合計成畝。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Fujian has much mountain farmland; scattered plots are combined in total to make full mu.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Fujian has much hillside land, with scattered plots totaled together to make full mu.

sentences.zh: 嗣後民間開墾不及一畝，與雖及一畝而地角山頭不相毗連者，免其昇科。

translations.literal: Hereafter, when common people open new land of less than one mu, or though reaching one mu the corner of the land and hilltop are not connected to each other, they should be exempted from tax upgrading.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth newly opened land of less than one mu, or land that reaches one mu but whose corners and hilltops are not contiguous, should be exempt from upgraded taxation.

sentences.zh: 」均從之。

translations.literal: " All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: " All were approved.

sentences.zh: 實授巡撫。

translations.literal: Formally appointed governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was formally appointed governor.

sentences.zh: 江蘇布政使安凝條奏賑務，上發各督撫察閱。

translations.literal: An Ning, provincial treasurer of Jiangsu, memorialized in detail on relief work; the Emperor sent it to all governors-general and governors for review.
translations.idiomatic: An Ning, provincial treasurer of Jiangsu, submitted a detailed memorial on relief work, which the Emperor circulated to all governors-general and governors for review.

sentences.zh: 恕疏言：「救災之法有三：曰賑，曰糶，曰借。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized: "There are three methods of disaster relief: called relief distribution, called relief sales, and called loans.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu memorialized: "There are three methods of disaster relief: relief distribution, relief sales, and loans.

sentences.zh: 此三者，實心辦理則益民，奉行不善則害政。

translations.literal: These three, if carried out in sincerity, benefit the people; if implemented poorly, they harm administration.
translations.idiomatic: Handled sincerely, these three benefit the people; handled badly, they harm government.

sentences.zh: 以賑而論，地方有司於倉猝查報時，分極貧、次貧。

translations.literal: Taking relief distribution: when local officials in haste investigate and report, they divide the extremely poor from the moderately poor.
translations.idiomatic: As for relief distribution, when local officials hurriedly investigate and report, they divide the extremely poor from the moderately poor.

sentences.zh: 一有差等，便啟弊端。

translations.literal: Once there are gradations, abuses are opened.
translations.idiomatic: Once gradations are introduced, abuses follow.

sentences.zh: 里甲於此酬恩怨，胥役於此得上下，而民之冀幸而生觖望者，更不待言。

translations.literal: Village headmen use this to settle old scores; clerks and runners use this to gain bribes; as for the people who hope and feel resentment, that need not even be mentioned.
translations.idiomatic: Village headmen settle old scores through it, clerks and runners take bribes through it, and the people's hopes and resentments need hardly be mentioned.

sentences.zh: 蓋貧富易辨，極次難分。

translations.literal: For riches and poverty are easy to distinguish, but extreme and moderate poverty are hard to separate.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and poverty are easy to tell apart, but extreme and moderate poverty are hard to distinguish.

sentences.zh: 如以有田為次貧，無田為極貧，一遇旱澇，顆粒皆無，有田與無田等也。

translations.literal: If taking those with fields as moderately poor and those without fields as extremely poor, when drought or flood strikes and not a grain remains, those with fields and those without are the same.
translations.idiomatic: If those with land are counted moderately poor and those without land extremely poor, then when drought or flood leaves not a grain behind, landholders and landless are alike.

sentences.zh: 如以有家為次貧，無家為極貧，則無從得食，相忍守飢，完聚與煢獨同也。

translations.literal: If taking those with homes as moderately poor and those without homes as extremely poor, then those with no means to obtain food endure hunger together; whether a family stays intact or a person is alone, it is the same.
translations.idiomatic: If those with homes are counted moderately poor and the homeless extremely poor, then when people have no food and endure hunger together, families intact and people alone suffer alike.

sentences.zh: 與其倉猝分別開爭競之門，莫如一視同仁絕覬覦之望。

translations.literal: Rather than in haste making distinctions and opening a gate to rivalry, better to treat all alike and cut off greedy expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than hurried distinctions that open the door to rivalry, it is better to treat all alike and remove the hope of favoritism.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為初賑似應一律散給，加賑再行分別，庶杜爭端。

translations.literal: This servant humbly thinks that initial relief should uniformly be distributed to all; additional relief may then make distinctions, so that disputes may be checked.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe that initial relief should be distributed equally to all, with distinctions made only in supplemental relief, so that disputes may be prevented.

sentences.zh: 以糶而論，定例石減時價一錢，俾小民升斗易求，牙商居奇無望，誠接濟良法。

translations.literal: Taking relief sales: the established rule reduces one cash per shi from the market price, so common people can easily buy by sheng and dou; grain brokers cannot corner the market in vain hope— truly a fine method of relief.
translations.idiomatic: As for relief sales, the established rule cuts one cash per shi from the market price so common people can easily buy grain by the measure and brokers cannot hoard in vain hope—it is truly an excellent method of relief.

sentences.zh: 乃有司每多請過減，倘輕聽準行，勢必希圖多糶，規利者云集喧囂。

translations.literal: Yet officials often frequently request reductions beyond the rule; if lightly approved, they will surely hope to sell more grain for profit, and those scheming for gain will gather in noisy crowds.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials often ask for deeper reductions than the rule allows; if these are lightly approved, they will seek to sell more grain for profit, and profiteers will gather in noisy crowds.

sentences.zh: 且米價太賤，商販不前。

translations.literal: Moreover, when rice prices are too low, merchants and peddlers do not come forward.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when rice prices fall too low, merchants stop bringing grain to market.

sentences.zh: 臣請嗣後平糶，仍照定例斟酌辦理，使災民實沾升斗之惠，而棍徒囤戶難行冒濫之姦。

translations.literal: Your servant requests that hereafter in relief sales, the established rule still be followed with careful discretion, so that disaster victims may truly receive the benefit of sheng and dou, while ruffians and hoarders cannot easily carry out fraudulent abuse.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that relief sales hereafter continue to follow the established rule with careful discretion, so that disaster victims truly receive grain by the measure while ruffians and hoarders cannot easily commit fraud.

sentences.zh: 以藉而論，動公家之銀，為百姓謀有無、通匱乏，此周官卹貧遺法也。

translations.literal: Taking loans: mobilizing public silver to plan for the people's needs and circulate shortages— this is the legacy method of the Rites of Zhou for relieving poverty.
translations.idiomatic: As for loans, using public funds to meet the people's needs and relieve shortages follows the ancient method of the Rites of Zhou for aiding the poor.

sentences.zh: 然使辦理未協，則官民交累。

translations.literal: Yet if implementation is not harmonious, officials and people burden each other.
translations.idiomatic: But if the work is not handled well, officials and people burden one another.

sentences.zh: 假如荒年田土無力耕種，有司借​​給耔種，猶可穫時即償。

translations.literal: Suppose in a famine year the fields cannot be cultivated for lack of strength; officials loan seed grain, and repayment can still be made at harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose that in a famine year people lack the strength to cultivate their fields; if officials lend seed grain, repayment can still be made at harvest.

sentences.zh: 若告貸銀米以給口食，則必計其能還而後與之，狡黠之流遂謂官​​有偏私，不免造謗生事。

translations.literal: If they borrow silver and grain for food, then it must be weighed whether they can repay before giving it; crafty people then say the officials show favoritism, and inevitably fabricate slander and stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: But if people borrow silver and grain for food, officials must consider whether they can repay before lending; crafty persons then accuse the officials of favoritism and inevitably spread slander and stir up trouble.

sentences.zh: 有司不得已略為變通，而無力還官，差拘徵比，民無安息。

translations.literal: Officials have no choice but to make slight adjustments; yet those unable to repay the government are rounded up and pressed for collection, and the people have no peace.
translations.idiomatic: Officials then make slight adjustments as a last resort, but those unable to repay the government are seized and pressed for payment, and the people know no peace.

sentences.zh: 是始則藉不能遍，因爭閧而被刑；

translations.literal: Thus at first because loans cannot reach everyone, they quarrel and are punished;
translations.idiomatic: At first loans cannot reach everyone, quarrels break out, and people are punished;

sentences.zh: 繼則還不能清，迫追呼而更困。

translations.literal: Then because repayment cannot be cleared, they are pressed by collection calls and become even more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: then repayment cannot be cleared, collection runners press them, and they are driven into greater hardship.

sentences.zh: 名為利民，實為病民。

translations.literal: Named as benefiting the people, in reality it harms the people.
translations.idiomatic: It is called benefiting the people, but in fact it harms them.

sentences.zh: 且年久不清，蒙恩豁免，帑項終歸無著。

translations.literal: Moreover, when debts remain unsettled for years and exemption is granted by imperial grace, the treasury funds ultimately have no whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when debts remain unsettled for years and are finally forgiven by imperial grace, the treasury ultimately loses track of the funds.

sentences.zh: 臣以為與其借而無償，莫如賑而不借。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that rather than lending without repayment, better to give relief and not lend.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that rather than lend without hope of repayment, it is better to give relief and not lend at all.

sentences.zh: 此皆當先事而熟籌者也。

translations.literal: All these should be carefully planned in advance.
translations.idiomatic: All of this should be carefully considered beforehand.

sentences.zh: 」報聞。

translations.literal: " The report was noted.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was noted.

sentences.zh: 旋以官按察使時刪改囚供，下吏部，召詣京師。

translations.literal: Soon, because as provincial judicial commissioner he had altered prisoners' confessions, the case was sent to the Board of Personnel and he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because while serving as provincial judicial commissioner he had altered prisoners' confessions, the case was sent to the Board of Personnel and he was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上以恕居官賢否詢閩浙總督策楞，又命新任巡撫劉於義考察。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Zongdu Celen of Fujian-Zhejiang about whether Shu was competent in office, and also ordered the newly appointed Governor Liu Yuyi to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Celen whether Wang Shu had served well, and also ordered the newly appointed governor Liu Yuyi to investigate.

sentences.zh: 策楞言「恕操守廉潔，老成持重，惟識力不能堅定」；

translations.literal: Celen said, "Shu is upright and incorrupt, mature and steady, but only his judgment cannot be firm";
translations.idiomatic: Celen reported, "Wang Shu is upright and incorrupt, mature and steady, but his judgment lacks firmness";

sentences.zh: 於義亦言「恕廉潔，百姓俱稱安靜和平，絕無擾累。

translations.literal: Yuyi also said, "Shu is incorrupt; the common people all call him quiet and peaceful, with absolutely no disturbance or burden.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuyi also reported, "Wang Shu is incorrupt; the people all praise him as quiet and peaceful, with no harassment or burden.

sentences.zh: 惟不能振作」。

translations.literal: Only he cannot invigorate [affairs]."
translations.idiomatic: Only he lacks vigor."

sentences.zh: 上謂兩奏皆至公之論。

translations.literal: The Emperor said both memorials were utterly fair judgments.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said that both reports were entirely fair.

sentences.zh: 尋補浙江布政使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed provincial treasurer of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed provincial treasurer of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 旋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 恕治事不苟。

translations.literal: Shu was not careless in handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu was never careless in handling affairs.

sentences.zh: 初授湖北糧道，押運赴淮，以船戶挾私鹽，自請總督糾劾。

translations.literal: When first appointed grain intendant of Hubei, escorting transport to Huai, because boatmen smuggled private salt, he himself requested the governor-general to impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first appointed grain intendant of Hubei and was escorting grain transport to Huai, he asked the governor-general to impeach boatmen who were smuggling private salt.

sentences.zh: 任江安糧道，整飭漕務尤有聲。

translations.literal: While serving as grain intendant of Jiang'an, he rectified grain transport duties with especial renown.
translations.idiomatic: As grain intendant of Jiang'an he reorganized grain transport with particular distinction.

sentences.zh: 充福建鄉試監臨，武生邱鵬飛以五經舉第一，士論不平，奏請覆試。

translations.literal: Serving as supervisor of the Fujian provincial examination, military licentiate Qiu Pengfei ranked first by passing all five classics; scholarly opinion was not satisfied, and he memorialized requesting a re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising the Fujian provincial examination, he saw military licentiate Qiu Pengfei rank first by passing all five classics; scholarly opinion was outraged, and Wang Shu memorialized for a re-examination.

sentences.zh: 尋察出實使其弟代作，吏議降調，上特寬之。

translations.literal: Soon it was discovered that he had actually had his younger brother compose [the papers]; the personnel office recommended demotion and transfer, but the Emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon discovered that Qiu had in fact had his younger brother write the papers for him; the personnel office recommended demotion and transfer, but the Emperor specially pardoned Wang Shu.

sentences.zh: 子汝璧，字鎮之。

translations.literal: His son Rubi, courtesy name Zhenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rubi, courtesy name Zhenzhi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年進士，授吏部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirty-first year of Qianlong, appointed a secretary in the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-first year of Qianlong and was appointed a secretary in the Board of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 出為直隸順德知府，調保定。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Shunde in Zhili, then transferred to Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Shunde in Zhili and later transferred to Baoding.

sentences.zh: 因承審建昌盜馬十未親鞫，奪官戍軍台。

translations.literal: Because in presiding over the trial of the Jianchang horse-theft case he did not personally interrogate [the prisoners], his office was stripped and he was sent to serve on the military colony.
translations.idiomatic: Because in presiding over the Jianchang horse-theft case he did not personally try the prisoners, he was stripped of office and sent to serve on the military colony.

sentences.zh: 尋準贖罪，降授同知，署直隸宣化府同知。

translations.literal: Soon permitted to redeem his offense, demoted and appointed sub-prefect, acting sub-prefect of Xuanhua in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon allowed to redeem his offense, was demoted to sub-prefect, and served as acting sub-prefect of Xuanhua in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 累擢大名道。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to intendant of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to intendant of Daming.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，擢山東按察使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, promoted to provincial judicial commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was promoted to provincial judicial commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, transferred to provincial treasurer of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 六年，護理巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 旋授安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon appointed governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 七年，請增設潁州督捕同知。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he requested the additional appointment of a sub-prefect for supervising bandit suppression at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he requested the creation of a sub-prefect at Yingzhou to supervise bandit suppression.

sentences.zh: 湖廣總督吳熊光等奏湖廣需兵米，請於安徽糴十萬石。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wu Xiongguang and others memorialized that Huguang needed military grain and requested purchase of 100,000 shi from Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Wu Xiongguang and others memorialized that Huguang needed military grain and asked to purchase 100,000 shi from Anhui.

sentences.zh: 上以安徽方缺雨，令酌量。

translations.literal: The Emperor, considering that Anhui was then short of rain, ordered that the amount be considered carefully.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, noting that Anhui was then suffering from drought, ordered that the amount be weighed carefully.

sentences.zh: 汝璧奏：「湖廣軍需事要，當如數撥運。

translations.literal: Rubi memorialized: "The military needs of Huguang are urgent matters; the full amount should be allocated and transported.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi memorialized: "Huguang's military needs are urgent and the full amount should be allocated and transported.

sentences.zh: 請視嘉慶二年例，先運六萬石。

translations.literal: I request that, following the precedent of the second year of Jiaqing, 60,000 shi be transported first.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that, following the precedent of the second year of Jiaqing, 60,000 shi be sent first.

sentences.zh: 」如所請。

translations.literal: " As requested.
translations.idiomatic: " His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 尋奏太湖續報成災，請緩徵，並劾府縣勘報遲延。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized that Taihu reported continuing disaster, requested deferred collection, and impeached the prefecture and counties for delay in investigation and report.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized that Taihu had again reported disaster, asked for deferred tax collection, and impeached the prefecture and counties for delay in surveying and reporting.

sentences.zh: 上以督撫查辦災賑，於奏報後續行查出災區，往往回護屬吏，將小民疾苦置之不問。

translations.literal: The Emperor said that when governors-general and governors handled disaster relief and investigation, after the memorial was submitted they often subsequently found disaster areas, frequently shielding subordinate officials and leaving the sufferings of common people unaddressed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said that when governors-general and governors investigated disaster relief, they often discovered additional disaster areas only after their initial reports, frequently shielding subordinates while ignoring the hardships of common people.

sentences.zh: 汝璧獨據實參奏，因深嘉之。

translations.literal: Rubi alone memorialized according to the facts, and for this was deeply commended.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi alone submitted a truthful memorial, and the Emperor greatly praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 八年，召授內閣學士，擢禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, summoned and appointed a Grand Secretariat academician, promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was summoned and appointed a Grand Secretariat academician, then promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 旋复授安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon again appointed governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon again appointed governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 九年，召授兵部侍郎，調刑部。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, summoned and appointed Vice Minister of War, transferred to the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of War, then transferred to the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 因病，請解任。

translations.literal: Because of illness, he requested release from office.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he asked to be relieved of his post.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year.

sentences.zh: 汝璧兄汝嘉，後汝璧六年成進士，官檢討。

translations.literal: Rubi's elder brother Rujia, six years after Rubi, became a jinshi and served as reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi's elder brother Rujia passed the jinshi examination six years after Rubi and served as a Hanlin reviser.

sentences.zh: =方顯=方顯，字週謨，湖南巴陵人。

translations.literal: Fang Xian, courtesy name Zhoumo, a native of Baling in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xian, courtesy name Zhoumo, was a native of Baling in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 自歲貢生授湘鄉教諭，稍遷廣西恭城知縣。

translations.literal: From senior licentiate he was appointed instructor of Xiangxiang, and was gradually promoted to magistrate of Gongcheng in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving his senior licentiate degree he was appointed instructor of Xiangxiang and was gradually promoted to magistrate of Gongcheng in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，詔諸行省舉賢能吏，布政使黃叔琬以顯應，超擢貴州鎮遠知府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, an edict ordered the provinces to recommend able officials; Provincial Treasurer Huang Shuwan recommended Xian, who was promoted over the regular course to prefect of Zhenyuan in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongzheng the throne ordered the provinces to recommend capable officials; Provincial Treasurer Huang Shuwan put forward Fang Xian, who was promoted out of turn to prefect of Zhenyuan in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 值歲饑，捐俸煮粥食饑民，民頌之。

translations.literal: When famine struck that year, he donated his salary to cook porridge for the hungry, and the people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck that year, he donated his salary to provide porridge for the hungry, and the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 總督鄂爾泰議開苗疆，改土歸流，雲南東川、烏蒙、鎮雄諸土府既內屬，貴州苗未服。

translations.literal: Governor-General Ortai proposed opening the Miao frontier and replacing native chieftains with regular administration; after the native prefectures of Dongchuan, Wumeng, and Zhenxiong in Yunnan had been brought under direct rule, the Miao of Guizhou had not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Ortai proposed opening the Miao frontier and replacing native chieftains with regular administration; after the native prefectures of Dongchuan, Wumeng, and Zhenxiong in Yunnan had been brought under direct rule, the Miao of Guizhou had not yet submitted.

sentences.zh: 貴州苗大者，南曰古州、曰八寨，西南曰丹江，東北曰九股、曰清水江。

translations.literal: Among the major Miao groups of Guizhou, to the south were Guzhou and Bazhai, to the southwest Danjiang, and to the northeast Jiugu and the Qingshui River.
translations.idiomatic: The major Miao groups of Guizhou lay to the south at Guzhou and Bazhai, to the southwest at Danjiang, and to the northeast at Jiugu and along the Qingshui River.

sentences.zh: 九股、清水江界鎮遠，丹江界凱里，八寨界都勻，古州界黎平，參錯萬山中，地方三千里，眾數十萬，恆出剽掠。

translations.literal: Jiugu and the Qingshui River bordered Zhenyuan; Danjiang bordered Kaili; Bazhai bordered Duyun; Guzhou bordered Liping; interspersed among myriad mountains, the region covered three thousand li, with populations of several hundred thousand, and they constantly raided and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Jiugu and the Qingshui River bordered Zhenyuan; Danjiang bordered Kaili; Bazhai bordered Duyun; and Guzhou bordered Liping. Scattered through myriad mountains across three thousand li, they numbered several hundred thousand and constantly raided and plundered.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰召顯問狀，顯力言宜如雲南例改土歸流。

translations.literal: Ortai summoned Xian and questioned him on conditions; Xian strongly argued that they should follow the Yunnan precedent of replacing native rule with direct administration.
translations.idiomatic: Ortai summoned Fang Xian to inquire into conditions, and Fang Xian strongly urged that the Yunnan precedent of replacing native rule with direct administration be followed.

sentences.zh: 問剿與撫宜孰施，對曰：「二者宜並施。

translations.literal: Asked whether suppression or conciliation should be applied, he replied: "Both should be applied together.
translations.idiomatic: When asked whether military suppression or conciliation should be used, he replied: "Both should be used together.

sentences.zh: 第先撫後剿，既剿則仍歸於撫耳。

translations.literal: Only conciliation first and suppression afterward; once suppression is done, one still returns to conciliation.
translations.idiomatic: But conciliation first and suppression afterward; and once suppression is done, one still returns to conciliation.

sentences.zh: 」因條上十六事，曰：別良頑，審先後，禁騷擾，耐繁難，防邀截，戒姑息，宥脅從，除漢奸，繳軍器，編戶口，輕錢糧，簡條約，設重兵，建城垣，分塘汛，疏河道，各為之說甚備，鄂爾泰韙之。

translations.literal: " He then submitted in detail sixteen points: distinguish the compliant from the stubborn, weigh priorities, forbid harassment, endure complexity, guard against ambush and interception, guard against undue leniency, pardon those coerced to follow, eliminate Han collaborators, collect weapons, register households, lighten taxes and grain levies, simplify regulations, deploy heavy garrisons, build walls, assign patrol posts, and dredge waterways; for each he gave explanations so thorough that Ortai approved them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then submitted sixteen detailed recommendations: distinguish the compliant from the stubborn, set priorities, forbid harassment, endure complexity, guard against ambush, avoid undue leniency, pardon those coerced to follow, eliminate Han collaborators, collect weapons, register households, lighten taxes and grain levies, simplify regulations, deploy heavy garrisons, build walls, assign patrol posts, and dredge waterways. His explanation of each point was so thorough that Ortai approved them.

sentences.zh: 檄按察使張廣泗招撫古州、丹江、八寨諸苗，而以九股、清水江諸苗屬顯。

translations.literal: An order was sent to Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Guangsi to conciliate and enroll the Miao of Guzhou, Danjiang, and Bazhai, while the Miao of Jiugu and the Qingshui River were assigned to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Guangsi was ordered to conciliate the Miao of Guzhou, Danjiang, and Bazhai, while the Miao of Jiugu and the Qingshui River were placed under Fang Xian.

sentences.zh: 六年，顯自樑上進次挨磨、者磨，再進次柏枝坪，宣諭諸苗，撫定清水江生苗十六寨、九股屬台拱生苗數寨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Xian advanced from Liangshang to encamp at Aimo and Zhemo, then advanced again to encamp at Baizhiping; he proclaimed the imperial message to the various Miao and pacified sixteen raw-Miao villages of the Qingshui River and several raw-Miao villages of Jiugu subordinate to Taigong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Fang Xian advanced from Liangshang to encamp at Aimo and Zhemo, then moved on to Baizhiping; he proclaimed the imperial message to the various Miao and pacified sixteen raw-Miao villages along the Qingshui River and several raw-Miao villages of Jiugu under Taigong.

sentences.zh: 冬，廣泗已戡定丹江，顯續招清水江生苗七寨、九股屬陶賴生苗十三寨。

translations.literal: In winter, Guangsi having already subdued Danjiang, Xian continued to enroll seven raw-Miao villages of the Qingshui River and thirteen raw-Miao villages of Taolai subordinate to Jiugu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, after Guangsi had subdued Danjiang, Fang Xian continued to enroll seven raw-Miao villages along the Qingshui River and thirteen raw-Miao villages of Taolai under Jiugu.

sentences.zh: 施秉有盜匿台拱農二寨，副將張尚謨捕不得，欲屠之。

translations.literal: At Shibing, bandits were hiding in two villages of Taigong farmers; Vice General Zhang Shangmo could not capture them and wished to massacre the villages.
translations.idiomatic: At Shibing, bandits were hiding in two Taigong farming villages; Vice General Zhang Shangmo could not capture them and wanted to massacre the villages.

sentences.zh: 苗懼，逃林谷，將為變。

translations.literal: The Miao were afraid, fled into forests and valleys, and were about to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao were terrified, fled into the forests and hills, and were on the verge of revolt.

sentences.zh: 顯聞之，曰：「如此則諸苗人人自危。

translations.literal: When Xian heard of this, he said: "If this is done, every Miao village will feel itself in danger.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Xian heard of this, he said: "If this is done, every Miao village will feel itself in danger.

sentences.zh: 」獨馳入苗寨，寨空無人，顯則宿寨中。

translations.literal: " He rode alone into the Miao village; the village was empty of people, yet Xian lodged in the village.
translations.idiomatic: " He rode alone into the Miao village. It was deserted, yet he spent the night there.

sentences.zh: 翌旦，張蓋出，令從者繞林谷呼苗出，撫諭之曰：「汝曹速歸寨即良民，天子必不殺良民。

translations.literal: The next morning, he went out under an umbrella and ordered his attendants to circle through the forests and valleys calling the Miao out; he conciliated and instructed them, saying: "If you return quickly to your villages you will be good subjects, and the Son of Heaven will surely not kill good subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he appeared under an umbrella and had his attendants search the forests and valleys, calling the Miao out; he reassured them, saying: "Return quickly to your villages and you will be loyal subjects, and the Son of Heaven will surely not kill loyal subjects.

sentences.zh: 」苗感泣，相率歸寨。

translations.literal: " The Miao wept in gratitude and returned to their villages in succession.
translations.idiomatic: " The Miao wept with gratitude and returned to their villages one after another.

sentences.zh: 顯益宿寨中三日，苗縛施秉盜以獻。

translations.literal: Xian lodged in the village for three more days, and the Miao bound up the Shibing bandits and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xian stayed in the village three more days, and the Miao bound the Shibing bandits and handed them over.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，廣泗以清水江南岸諸寨尚懷觀望，檄顯與尚謨率兵循北岸徼巡。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year, because the villages on the south bank of the Qingshui River still wavered, Guangsi ordered Xian and Shangmo to lead troops patrolling along the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year, because villages on the south bank of the Qingshui River still held back, Guangsi ordered Fang Xian and Shangmo to lead troops on patrol along the north bank.

sentences.zh: 次柳羅，南岸公鵝、柳利、雞擺尾諸寨苗渡江來攻，顯督兵御之，殺數十人。

translations.literal: Encamped at Liuluo, Miao from the south-bank villages of Gong'e, Liuli, and Jibaiwei crossed the river to attack; Xian directed the troops in defense and killed several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: While encamped at Liuluo, Miao from the south-bank villages of Gong'e, Liuli, and Jibaiwei crossed the river to attack; Fang Xian directed the defense and killed several dozen men.

sentences.zh: 苗眾師寡，尚謨欲引退，顯不可，固守待援。

translations.literal: The Miao were many and the army few; Shangmo wished to withdraw, but Xian would not allow it and held firm awaiting relief.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao greatly outnumbered the troops; Shangmo wanted to retreat, but Fang Xian refused and held his ground awaiting reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 廣泗師至，圍乃解。

translations.literal: When Guangsi's army arrived, the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangsi's troops arrived, the encirclement was broken.

sentences.zh: 廣泗用顯議，散諸寨，專攻公鵝，破之，諸寨皆聽命。

translations.literal: Guangsi adopted Xian's plan, dispersed the other villages, and concentrated the attack on Gong'e; once it was taken, all the villages submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi adopted Fang Xian's plan, dispersed the other villages, and concentrated on Gong'e; once it fell, all the villages submitted.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰奏置貴東道，即以命顯，仍駐兵清江。

translations.literal: Ortai memorialized to establish the Guidong circuit, and Xian was appointed to it, still stationing troops at Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ortai memorialized to establish the Guidong circuit, and Fang Xian was appointed to it while keeping troops stationed at Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 顯申軍令，誓將士毋掠，毋淫，毋踐田穀，苗民有來愬者，為處其曲直；

translations.literal: Xian announced military orders, swearing the officers and soldiers not to plunder, not to commit licentious acts, and not to trample the fields and grain; when Miao people came to lodge complaints, he judged right and wrong for them;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xian issued military orders, binding officers and soldiers not to plunder, not to commit outrages, and not to trample crops; when Miao people came with grievances, he judged their disputes;

sentences.zh: 乃益築城郭，建官廨，治砲台​​營房，苗民競來助役。

translations.literal: he then further built walls and cities, erected official quarters, and constructed batteries and barracks, and Miao people competed to come and assist in the labor.
translations.idiomatic: he then built walls and cities, erected government offices, and constructed batteries and barracks, and Miao people eagerly came to help with the work.

sentences.zh: 九年，諸工竟。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, all the works were completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year all the construction was finished.

sentences.zh: 顯巡行視塘汛，黔、楚商船上下相接，苗民皆悅服。

translations.literal: Xian toured and inspected the patrol posts; merchant boats of Guizhou and Huguang passed up and down in unbroken succession, and the Miao people were all pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xian toured the patrol posts; merchant boats from Guizhou and Huguang passed up and down without interruption, and the Miao were fully won over.

sentences.zh: 事粗定，尋授顯按察使。

translations.literal: When affairs were roughly settled, he was soon appointed provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Once affairs were roughly settled, he was soon appointed provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 台拱者，苗中扼要地也，鄂爾泰議置營於此。

translations.literal: Taigong was a strategic point among the Miao; Ortai proposed establishing a garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: Taigong was a strategic point in Miao territory, and Ortai proposed establishing a garrison there.

sentences.zh: 十年，巡撫張廣泗奏請顯董其事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Governor Zhang Guangsi memorialized requesting that Xian supervise the undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Governor Zhang Guangsi memorialized asking that Fang Xian direct the project.

sentences.zh: 秋，羊翁、烏羅、桃賴諸寨苗為亂，九股諸苗附之，攻台拱。

translations.literal: In autumn, the Miao of the villages of Yangweng, Wuluo, and Taolai rebelled; the Miao of Jiugu joined them and attacked Taigong.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Miao of Yangweng, Wuluo, Taolai, and other villages rebelled; the Jiugu Miao joined them and attacked Taigong.

sentences.zh: 顯與總兵趙文英嚴為備，擊走之。

translations.literal: Xian and Regional Commander Zhao Wenying made strict preparations and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xian and Regional Commander Zhao Wenying made thorough preparations and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 進破羊翁寨。

translations.literal: Advancing, they took Yangweng village.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing forward, they captured Yangweng village.

sentences.zh: 苗夜至，顯以兵少，令人爇兩炷香手之為火繩狀以怖苗，苗走，退踞排略。

translations.literal: The Miao came by night; because his troops were few, Xian had men burn two sticks of incense and carry them in their hands in the shape of slow-match cords to frighten the Miao; the Miao fled and withdrew to occupy Pailue.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao attacked by night; with too few troops, Fang Xian had men burn two sticks of incense and carry them like slow-match cords to frighten the enemy; the Miao fled and withdrew to hold Pailue.

sentences.zh: 排略者台拱隘，我師餉道所必經。

translations.literal: Pailue was a pass at Taigong through which the army's supply route had to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Pailue was a pass at Taigong through which the army's supply route had to pass.

sentences.zh: 台拱師僅二千五百人，苗數万，援兵再敗。

translations.literal: The garrison at Taigong had only twenty-five hundred men, while the Miao numbered tens of thousands, and relief troops were twice defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Taigong garrison had only twenty-five hundred men against tens of thousands of Miao, and relief columns were defeated twice.

sentences.zh: 自賊始攻，或欲棄之走，顯拒之。

translations.literal: From the time the rebels first attacked, some wished to abandon the place and flee, but Xian refused.
translations.idiomatic: From the first rebel attack some wanted to abandon the post and flee, but Fang Xian refused.

sentences.zh: 及圍久糧盡，宰馬以食，迫冬寒，眾洶洶不自保，議潰圍退保下秉。

translations.literal: When the siege dragged on and grain was exhausted, they slaughtered horses for food; as winter cold pressed in, the men grew restless and could not feel secure, and there was talk of breaking out of the encirclement and withdrawing to defend Xiabing.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege wore on and provisions ran out, they slaughtered horses for food; with winter cold setting in the men grew restless and insecure, and some proposed breaking out and falling back to defend Xiabing.

sentences.zh: 顯曰：「台拱失，古州、清江諸寨皆煽動。

translations.literal: Xian said: "If Taigong is lost, the villages of Guzhou, Qingjiang, and the rest will all be stirred up.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xian said: "If Taigong falls, the villages of Guzhou, Qingjiang, and the rest will all be stirred up.

sentences.zh: 苟免，失臣節；

translations.literal: To seek escape would be to fail in a minister's duty;
translations.idiomatic: To seek escape would be to fail in a minister's duty;

sentences.zh: 撓敗，損國威。

translations.literal: to yield defeat would damage the state's prestige.
translations.idiomatic: to yield defeat would damage the state's prestige.

sentences.zh: 事急，死此耳。

translations.literal: When matters are urgent, one dies here—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: When matters are urgent, one dies here—that is all.

sentences.zh: 」眾感奮，會總兵霍升援至。

translations.literal: " The men were moved and roused; just then Regional Commander Huo Sheng's relief arrived.
translations.idiomatic: " The men were stirred to fight on; just then relief under Regional Commander Huo Sheng arrived.

sentences.zh: 苗奪我後山，樵路絕，顯夜出兵奪以還。

translations.literal: The Miao seized our rear hill, cutting off the firewood route; Xian sent troops out by night and recaptured it.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao seized the rear hill and cut off the firewood route; Fang Xian sent troops out by night and recaptured it.

sentences.zh: 苗攻益急，顯怒馬擊之，眾殊死戰，苗敗走。

translations.literal: As the Miao pressed their attack ever harder, Xian charged them on horseback in anger; the men fought to the death, and the Miao were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: As the Miao pressed their attack, Fang Xian charged them on horseback in fury; his men fought to the death and the Miao were routed.

sentences.zh: 乘勝拔烏孟、井底二寨，取米穀餉軍。

translations.literal: Following up the victory, they took the two villages of Wumeng and Jingdi and seized grain to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Following up the victory, they took the villages of Wumeng and Jingdi and seized grain to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 升兵亦克大關入，顯率兵出夾擊，苗大潰。

translations.literal: Huo Sheng's troops also broke through at Daguan and entered; Xian led his troops out in a pincer attack, and the Miao were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Sheng's troops also broke through at Daguan; Fang Xian led his men out in a pincer attack and the Miao were utterly routed.

sentences.zh: 凡堅守六十九日而圍解。

translations.literal: In all they held firm for sixty-nine days before the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In all they held out for sixty-nine days before the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 提督哈元生師繼至，破蓮花悍苗。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Ha Yuansheng's army arrived in succession and broke the fierce Miao at Lianhua.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Ha Yuansheng's troops arrived in succession and defeated the fierce Miao at Lianhua.

sentences.zh: 九股苗复定。

translations.literal: The Jiugu Miao were again pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiugu Miao were pacified once more.

sentences.zh: 自鄂爾泰議開貴州苗疆，事發於廣泗，而策決於顯，卒終始其事，崎嶇前後七年而事集。

translations.literal: From the time Ortai proposed opening the Guizhou Miao frontier, the affair was launched by Guangsi while the strategy was decided by Xian; in the end he saw the matter through from beginning to end, and over seven arduous years the undertaking was completed.
translations.idiomatic: From Ortai's proposal to open the Guizhou Miao frontier, the campaign was launched by Guangsi while the strategy was Fang Xian's; in the end he saw the matter through from start to finish, and after seven arduous years the undertaking was completed.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，丁母憂，去官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, upon his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong, upon his mother's death he left office.

sentences.zh: 三年，服除，授四川布政使。

translations.literal: In the third year, when mourning ended, he was appointed provincial treasurer of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when his mourning ended, he was appointed provincial treasurer of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 四年，署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 大小金川、雜穀、梭磨、沃日、革布什咱諸土司相仇殺，顯遣人諭之，事稍解。

translations.literal: The native chieftains of Greater and Lesser Jinchuan, Zagun, Suomo, Wori, and Gebushizan were mutually feuding and killing one another; Xian sent men to instruct them, and the trouble was somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: The native chieftains of Greater and Lesser Jinchuan, Zagun, Suomo, Wori, and Gebushizan were feuding and killing one another; Fang Xian sent envoys to instruct them, and the trouble eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 議者欲乘此視雲南、貴州例，令改土歸流。

translations.literal: Some advisers wished to seize the occasion, following the Yunnan and Guizhou precedents, to replace native rule with direct administration.
translations.idiomatic: Some advisers wanted to take the opportunity, following the Yunnan and Guizhou precedents, to replace native rule with direct administration.

sentences.zh: 顯疏言：「雜穀、梭磨，吐番後裔，其巢穴在唐為維州，戶口十餘萬。

translations.literal: Xian memorialized, stating: "Zagun and Suomo are descendants of the Tibetans; their strongholds were Weizhou under the Tang, with households numbering more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xian memorialized, stating: "Zagun and Suomo are descendants of Tibetans; their strongholds were Weizhou under the Tang, with more than one hundred thousand households.

sentences.zh: 金川與接壤，戶口不過數万。

translations.literal: Jinchuan borders them, with households numbering no more than several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jinchuan borders them, with no more than several tens of thousands of households.

sentences.zh: 雜穀憚金川之強，金川則畏雜穀之眾，彼此箝制，邊境乂安。

translations.literal: Zagun fears Jinchuan's strength, while Jinchuan dreads Zagun's numbers; each restrains the other, and the frontier is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Zagun fears Jinchuan's strength while Jinchuan dreads Zagun's numbers; each checks the other, and the frontier remains at peace.

sentences.zh: 固不可任其爭競，亦不可強其和協。

translations.literal: One certainly cannot allow them to struggle and compete at will, yet one also cannot force them into harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Their rivalry cannot be left unchecked, yet they cannot be forced into harmony either.

sentences.zh: 沿邊生番，留之可為內地捍衛。

translations.literal: The raw tribes along the frontier, if kept in place, can serve as a defense for the interior.
translations.idiomatic: The raw tribes along the frontier, if kept in place, can serve as a bulwark for the interior.

sentences.zh: 從前川省調用土兵，亦供徵發。

translations.literal: In former times when Sichuan mobilized native troops, they also supplied levies for campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: In former times when Sichuan mobilized native troops, they also supplied levies for campaigns.

sentences.zh: 至其同類操戈，原未擾及內地。

translations.literal: When they fought one another with weapons, they had not in the first place disturbed the interior.
translations.idiomatic: When they fought one another, they had not in the first place disturbed the interior.

sentences.zh: 前經化誨，亦尚凜遵。

translations.literal: After earlier instruction and admonition, they still observed the rules with awe.
translations.idiomatic: After earlier instruction and admonition, they still observed the rules with due respect.

sentences.zh: 設欲改土歸流，非惟彈丸土司無裨尺寸，且所給印信號紙，一經追取，即成無統屬之生番。
